key_insight: Aligning single white blood cell images with genetic information (karyotype and mutations) creates richer patient representations that improve hematological diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This approach better matches how blood cancer diagnosis is done in practice, where morphology is interpreted alongside cytogenetic and molecular test results.
method: Self-supervised pretraining of a vision transformer aggregator on more than 1,500 patients using an iBOT head.
Supervised contrastive genetic alignment on acute myeloid leukemia patients with chromosomal aberration and gene panel data.
Resulting patient encoder supports diagnosis and retrieval of diseases and genetic alterations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved performance on hematological diagnostic tasks, outperforming slide-level histopathology foundation models, using a cohort of over 1,500 patients for pretraining and AML cases for genetic alignment.
watch_item: The alignment strategy depends on paired genetic and image data, which may limit deployment where cytogenetic or sequencing results are incomplete or unavailable.
paper_title: Genetically Aligned Patient Representations Improve Hematological Diagnosis
